newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Life to be biggest buyer of NCB new shares.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Life to be biggest buyer of NCB new shares.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Life Insurance Co will be the biggest buyer of new shares due to be issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), with a planned purchase of 114.68 million shares worth 25 billion yen, according to the list of buyers released by NCB on Thursday.
Nippon Life is among 33 Japanese financial institutions due to purchase the troubled Japanese bank's 766.04 million new shares, worth 167 billion yen, in a third-party allotment.
NCB said on Tuesday that the new shares will be priced at 218 yen each, and that the buyers had informally agreed to hold the new NCB shares for two years from the issuance.
The payment date is June 30, it said.

Industrial Bank of Japan plans to buy 77.98 million NCB shares for 17 billion yen, making it the second biggest buyer, followed by Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd which plans to buy 55.05 million shares for 12 billion yen. The two banks, like NCB, are long-term credit banks.
Other buyers are 10 Japanese major "city" banks, seven non-life insurance companies, and 13 life insurers.
In addition to the planned new share issue, NCB is also considering raising capital by 123.7 billion yen by issuing preferred stock.
